paragraphs.text: DSH plugin: bridges DeepSeek Harness session status to the DSH Status macOS menu bar app.
# DSH Status Bridge

A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that bridges
session status from DSH to the DSH Status
macOS menu ba

r app, and forwards "jump to session" commands from the app back
into DSH.
The plugin has two halves:
| File | Role |
| `index.js` | Host bridge: registers the `/dsh-status` routes (state / SSE / commands), listens for
`turn/end` to tell completed from stopped turns, writes `~/.dsh-status/bridge.json`, and optionally

launches the app |
| `client.js` | Client half (runs inside the DSH renderer, no UI): aggregates `u
iSession` / `sessions` / `workspaces` state and pushes it to the host; long-polls for `uiWorkspace.o

penSession` commands |
| `lib/aggregate.js` | Pure functions: state derivation, counting and snapsho

t validation (shared by the host and the tests) |
| `test/` | `node --test` unit tests plus host-rou
te integration tests and a fake-context client test |
## Requirements

- macOS (the companion app is a menu bar app)
- DSH desktop **0.2.1-rc.5** or newer in the 0.2.x lin

e (verified on `0.2.1-rc.5`
and `0.2.2-rc.1`)
- Node.js **>= 20** (bundled with DSH, nothing to inst

all manually)
- The companion app installed first: dsh-status releases
## Install

1. Install the **DSH Status** app (DMG → drag to `/Applications`, or the install
script places it in

`~/Applications`).
2. In DSH: sidebar **Plugins** → **Add plugin** → **Install a third-party plugin

**
→ enter the package name `dsh-status-bridge` → **Install** → **Enable now**.
If the npm package i

s not available from your registry yet, paste the Git URL
`github:HAppy-2436/dsh-status-bridge` in t

he same field instead.
3. The plugin writes `~/.dsh-status/bridge.json` and tries to launch the app;

the
whale / segmented-ring icon should appear in the menu bar.
4. Clicking a session row in the app
panel jumps to that session in DSH.
If the app was not launched automatically, start it manually once.

1. `config.appPath`
2. `DSH_STATUS_APP` environment variable
3. `/Applications/DSH Status.app`
4. `~
/Applications/DSH Status.app`
Environment variables (development only):

- `DSH_STATUS_DIR` — override the directory holding `bridge.json`
(default `~/.dsh-status`).

`bridge.json` is versioned (`version: 1`) and contains `pluginVersion`; the app
ignores unknown keys
, so plugin and app can be upgraded independently.
## Compatibility
| DSH | Status |

| `0.2.1-rc.5` | verified on device |
| `0.2.2-rc.1` | verified on device |
| older than `0.2.1-rc.5
` or `>= 0.3.0` | unsupported (declared in `engines.dsh`) |
## Session filtering
Only **top-level** sessions are counted, displayed and notified:

- subagent sessions (`origin === 'subagent'`, or sessions with a parent) are
listed indented in the
ank sessions are ignored.
## Titles

Session titles come from the Session `title` projection (list rows may lag or be
empty):

- the client half calls `ctx.sessions.refreshProjections(sessionId)` when a title
is missing (at mos

Of(session, 'title')` for running sessions;
- the app shows "Untitled session" when nothing is avail

ssion, 'title')` for running sessions;
- the app shows "Untitled session" when nothing is available.
## Known limitations

- `completionUnread` on the client is renderer-memory state: unread counts reset
after a DSH restart

(same as DSH's own badges).
- With multiple windows/tabs each client pushes its own snapshot; the h

ost keeps
the last push (single-window assumption).
- The host only sees `turn/end` events that happ

en after the plugin starts;
sessions finished before that are treated as completed.

docs/protocol.md. Any field change

must update that document
first.
## Publishing

Releases are published from tags by `.github/workflows/publish.yml` using npm
**Trusted Publishing (
OIDC)** — no long-lived token, no OTP:

1. Configure the package's Trusted Publisher on npmjs.com once
(**Settings → Trusted Publisher**): G

itHub Actions, owner `HAppy-2436`,
repository `dsh-status-bridge`, workflow filename `publish.yml`,

allow
`npm publish`.
2. Then push a version tag:

The workflow runs the checks and publishes with a short-lived OIDC token
(`id-token: write`) plus au

tomatic provenance. It never publishes from a local
machine.
